CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  MARCH 24, 2026

A special meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Torosis at 5:35 p.m., on
Tuesday, March 24, 2026, at City Council Chambers, 1685 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA.

Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Caroline Torosis
  Mayor Pro Tern Jesse Zwick
  Councilmember Lana Negrete
  Councilmember Dan Hall
  Councilmember Ellis Raskin
  Councilmember Barry Snell
  Councilmember Natalya Zemitskaya

  Also Present:  City Manager Oliver Chi
  City Attorney Heidi von Tongeln
  Interim City Clerk Denise Anderson-Warren

CONVENE/PLEDGE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened at 5:35 p.m., with all
  members present. Councilmember Raskin led the assemblage in the Pledge
  of Allegiance.

STATEMENT OF  The City of Santa Monica Statement of Accountability (Land
ACCOUNTABILITY  Acknowledgement) was read into the record by Councilmember
(LAND  Zemitskaya.
ACKNOWLEDGEMENT)

LEVINE ACT  No Councilmembers made disclosures regarding the Levine Act (Govt Code
DISCLOSURE  Section 84308).

PUBLIC INPUT  Members of the public Andrew Hoyer, Clare Thomas, John C. Smith, and
  Elizabeth van Denburg commented on item 16.A.

COUNCILMEMBER  In accordance with Council Rule 6(y), all Councilmember Discussion items
DISCUSSION ITEMS:  were considered and approved in one motion unless removed by a
  Councilmember for discussion.

NEIGHBORHOOD  16.A. Request of Mayor Torosis, Councilmember Hall and
ORGANIZATION GRANT  Councilmember Raskin to Direct Staff to Review and Clarify
PROGRAM GUIDANCE  Neighborhood Organization Grant Program Guidance, was presented.

  Motion by Councilmember Hall, seconded by Mayor Torosis, to approve the
  recommendation to include the following:

  1  March 24, 2026
 The City Council direct staff to:
  1. Review the unanimous Council direction from September 30, 2025
  regarding the Neighborhood Organization Grant Program,
  confirming that public funds not be used to take positions on political
  candidates;
  2. Ensure that the program application, guidelines, and related materials
  are fully consistent with Council direction;
  3. Refine and clarify program guidance, including through updated
  application materials and Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs), to
  explicitly state that:
  a. Neighborhood organizations may conduct education and outreach
  related to ballot measures, provided such activities are informational
  in nature;
  b. The use of funds for communications, including mailers, to inform
  members about meetings, events, and programming is permissible;
  c. Organizations are required to submit a proposed annual budget at
  the beginning of the grant period, consistent with prior practice, and
  are not required to obtain pre-approval for each individual
  expenditure;
  d. Neighborhood organizations may host meetings between their
  members and individuals running for office, provided such activities
  are conducted in a neutral and information-sharing manner;
  e. Any requests for demographic information from participating
  organizations or their members are strictly voluntary;
  4. Confirm that Neighborhood Organizations may form or operate
  separate affiliated entities to perform political activities;
  5. Clarify the City Council's intent that if a Neighborhood Association
  forms or operates an affiliated entity to exercise their First
  Amendment right to endorse political candidates, that entity cannot
  receive taxpayer resources or participate in the City's Neighborhood
  Organization Grant Program;
  6. Reaffirm that Neighborhood Organizations participating in the
  City's grant program should be entities that are engaged in the
  performance of civic community building functions;
  7. Confirm that only those groups that qualify, apply, and are
  identified as an official Neighborhood Organization will be listed
  by the City as an official participant of the City's Neighborhood
  Association Grant Program;
  8. Further, confirm that elected officials and staff are not barred from
  meeting with groups who choose to endorse political candidates in
  their official capacity as representatives of the City to give briefings
  or answer questions;
  9. Return with any additional recommendations necessary to ensure
  clarity, accessibility, and consistency in program implementation;
  and

  2  March 24, 2026
   10.  Following the release of updated application materials and FAQs,
  re-open the application period for the 2025-26 Neighborhood
  Organization Grant Program to allow interested organizations to
  apply in light of the clarified guidance.

  The motion was approved by a 6-1 voice vote, with Councilmember Negrete
  voting no.

ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the City Council special meeting adjourned at 12:18
  a.m.
